key_insight: LLM reasoning performance is associated with stronger small-world functional connectivity in attention-head activation graphs, especially higher clustering and shorter paths.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a structural way to diagnose and preserve reasoning ability in LLMs, and it can guide pruning/allocation methods that keep important internal connectivity intact.
method: Build functional graphs from attention-head activation similarity across models and checkpoints.
Measure small-world index (SWI) plus per-head core and bridge scores to identify important heads.
Use these scores in Small-World Allocation (SWA) to guide hierarchical sparsity and pruning.
evidence_signal: Across six LLMs, higher SWI correlated with better fluid reasoning, and SWA preserved performance and small-world structure while reducing WikiText perplexity by up to 20%.
watch_item: The findings are correlational and depend on how functional graphs, similarity metrics, and pruning scores are constructed, so generalization to other architectures or tasks should be tested.
paper_title: Looking Inside LLMs: Small-World Connectivity as a Signature of Reasoning Performance
